study type: Retrospective policy evaluation using a difference-in-differences quasi-experimental design
exposure: Voluntary pledge policy to reduce early-term elective deliveries
Mandatory nonpayment policy to reduce early-term elective deliveries
outcome: Probability of an early elective delivery (EED)
Proportion of births occurring before 39 weeks
Proportion of babies born with low birthweight
cohort: The cohort consisted of privately insured and Medicaid-enrolled individuals with births recorded in birth certificate data from South Carolina and 16 control states between 2009 and 2015.
finding: Both voluntary pledge and mandatory nonpayment policies were effective in reducing overall early elective delivery rates, with mandatory policies showing a greater impact and larger relative decreases observed among Medicaid enrollees.
